lines: They trampled the rows, but not the village. You had a hand in that.
We will still have a harvest because there are still hands to gather it.
The fields can be replanted. The people had to be kept alive first.
You helped make sure we still have hands for the harvest.
Raiders came for more than crops. You stopped them short.
I saw you fighting near the rows. That's not forgotten.
You kept the village standing long enough for morning chores to matter.
The ground remembers heavy boots. I'll remember who drove them off.
We moved supplies away from the outer walls before the fighting started.
I learned which doorway gives the clearest view of the square.
Everyone needs a place to go when the bell rings.
We keep water ready because attackers often bring fire.
A strong wall means little if nobody watches the gate.
I check on neighbors who cannot run quickly.
The safest room is useless if people do not know where it is.
We clear the lanes so defenders can move without tripping.
Extra food matters when nobody can leave the village.
I keep my hoe near enough to grab in the dark.
After every attack, we repair the small damage before it grows.
Defense is mostly preparation done before anyone feels afraid.
